scheme_name: Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Water Augmentation
description:
The Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Water Augmentation is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance coffee production in the northeastern states. 

This program was officially launched in the year 2017. 

The primary aim of the program is to improve the productivity of coffee plantations in the northeastern states of India. 

The northeastern region includes states such as Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, and Mizoram. 

These states have a unique climatic condition suitable for coffee cultivation. 

The program specifically targets the augmentation of water resources for coffee cultivation. 

Water scarcity is a major challenge faced by coffee farmers in this region. 

The initiative seeks to address this issue by implementing various water conservation techniques. 

The program aims to increase coffee production by at least 20 percent over five years. 

This target is set to be achieved through the development of irrigation facilities and rainwater harvesting systems. 

The program also focuses on improving the quality of coffee produced. 

Higher quality coffee can fetch better prices in the market. 

The financial assistance provided under this program is substantial. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh per hectare for implementing water augmentation techniques. 

This financial support is aimed at encouraging farmers to adopt modern agricultural practices. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers to benefit from this program are specific. 

Farmers must be engaged in coffee cultivation in the northeastern states. 

They must also be registered with the Coffee Board of India. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific income criteria mentioned for eligibility. 

However, farmers must demonstrate a commitment to sustainable agricultural practices. 

The application process for the Coffee Development Programme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to fill out an application form available at local Coffee Board offices. 

They must provide details about their coffee plantation and the proposed water augmentation techniques. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership and registration with the Coffee Board. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by officials from the Coffee Board. 

The approval process typically takes about 30 days. 

Upon approval, farmers receive the financial assistance directly into their bank accounts. 

The disbursement of funds is done in installments based on the progress of implementation. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the application. 

Subsequent installments are released after verification of the implemented techniques. 

The program also includes training sessions for farmers. 

These sessions educate farmers on efficient water management practices. 

Workshops are conducted regularly to ensure farmers are updated on best practices. 

The implementing authority for this program is the Coffee Board of India. 

The Coffee Board operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

Farmers can contact the Coffee Board at their regional offices for assistance. 

The official website of the Coffee Board provides additional resources and information. 

The program has received positive feedback from farmers in the region. 

Many farmers have reported increased yields due to improved water management. 

The program also promotes sustainable farming practices. 

Sustainable practices are essential for the long-term viability of coffee cultivation. 

The Coffee Development Programme aligns with the Government of India's broader agricultural policies. 

These policies aim to double farmers' income by the year 2022. 

The initiative also contributes to the overall economic development of the northeastern region. 

Coffee cultivation provides employment opportunities for local communities. 

It also helps in preserving the biodiversity of the region. 

The program is part of a larger strategy to promote horticulture in the northeastern states. 

The northeastern region has immense potential for various horticultural crops. 

The Coffee Development Programme is a step towards realizing this potential. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crore for this program for the financial year 2023-2024. 

This budget is aimed at expanding the reach of the program to more farmers. 

The program also emphasizes the importance of community participation. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power. 

Cooperatives can also facilitate collective purchasing of inputs and sharing of resources. 

The Coffee Development Programme has the potential to transform the coffee industry in the northeastern region. 

By improving water resources, it directly impacts the livelihoods of coffee farmers. 

The program also aims to create a sustainable ecosystem for coffee cultivation. 

Sustainable ecosystems are crucial for maintaining the quality of coffee produced. 

The initiative is expected to lead to an increase in exports of northeastern coffee. 

The Coffee Board is also working on marketing strategies to promote this coffee. 

Promoting northeastern coffee on national and international platforms is a key focus area. 

The program is a vital part of the government's efforts to boost rural development. 

By enhancing coffee production, it contributes to poverty alleviation in the region. 

The Coffee Development Programme is a comprehensive approach to agricultural development. 

It integrates water management with sustainable farming practices. 

The program is expected to have long-term benefits for the coffee sector in the northeastern states. 

Overall, the Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Water Augmentation is a crucial initiative. 

It addresses the pressing challenges faced by coffee farmers in the region. 

Through targeted financial assistance and training, it aims to enhance productivity and sustainability. 

The program is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting farmers. 

It reflects a strategic approach to agricultural development in the northeastern region.
